astra.act1.battery_built: Heating core online! Out on the surface tonight it will drop to about minus 80 degrees Celsius. Our trick: we catch the leftover heat every machine makes and send it to your rooms. NASA's Perseverance rover stays warm the same way, using spare heat from its power generator.
astra.act1.drone02_wake: Drone #02 is back online! Two builders means we can build two rooms at the same time. Teamwork!
astra.act1.end: We survived our first week on Mars! Next, let's grow food and get the Rover rolling. Pathfinder-X's last message is still out there somewhere.
astra.act1.first_dusk: The Sun is setting. Tonight it can drop to about minus 80 degrees Celsius outside. Keep an eye on the Heat bar!
astra.act1.first_sleep: Good morning! Sleeping in the Bedroom gave you back 12 HP. Rest is a real part of every space mission.
astra.act1.first_sunset: Look, a blue sunset! On Mars, fine dust scatters the light so sunsets glow blue, the opposite of Earth.
astra.act1.heat_warning: Brrr! The base is losing heat. Let's reroute the warm pipes before it gets colder.
astra.act1.repair_kit_ready: Repair Kit done! Drag it onto Drone #02 to fix its dusty joints.
astra.act1.storm_begin: Here it comes! The sky is turning dark orange. Dust storms on Mars can grow big enough to cover the whole planet.
astra.act1.storm_end: The storm is over! Time to clean up. Mars dust is super fine and sticks to everything, like a balloon to your hair.
astra.act1.storm_mid: Our panels are only getting a trickle of sunlight. Every bit of saved power helps.
astra.act1.title: ACT I: WAKE UP
astra.act1.workshop_built: Workshop ready! Mars is too far away to order spare parts, so we'll make our own. In 2014, astronauts on the International Space Station 3D-printed a wrench from a design emailed up from Earth. First job: a Repair Kit for Drone #02!
astra.act1.workshop_start: Next up: the Workshop. If something breaks on Mars, we can't call a repair shop. We make the parts ourselves.
astra.act2.blackbox_home: The black box is safe in the Garage, but it's locked with an old code. We need a working Comms Lab to read it.
astra.act2.drone03_wake: Drone #03 reporting for duty! All three builders are awake. Now we can really get moving.
astra.act2.end: Three drones, a garden, a Rover and a mystery box. Not bad! Next, let's get the Lab online and find out what Pathfinder-X heard.
astra.act2.first_harvest: First harvest: fresh lettuce! In 2015, astronauts on the space station ate lettuce they grew in space. Fresh food now gives you extra HP every Sol.
astra.act2.garage_built: The Rover is ready to roll! Drive carefully: Mars rocks are sharp. NASA's Curiosity rover got holes and cracks in its metal wheels from them. Clean wheels, careful driving!
astra.act2.garage_start: Drone #02 is on the Garage & Airlock. Soon we can send the Rover out to explore!
astra.act2.greenhouse_built: Greenhouse growing! Martian soil has perchlorates, salty chemicals that are bad for people, so we skip the dirt. NASA's Phoenix lander found them in 2008. Our plants grow in water mixed with plant food, under red and blue LEDs, the colors plants use most.
astra.act2.greenhouse_start: Drone #01 is building the Greenhouse. Fresh food will keep your energy up, and plants make oxygen too!
astra.act2.map_intro: This is the holographic crater map. Tap a glowing spot to send the Rover. It drives off-screen, and I'll keep you posted by radio.
astra.act2.pathfinder_found: Commander, look, that's Pathfinder-X! It's been waiting here since 2038. Grab its black box, it recorded everything before the storm. And its big antenna could fix our Comms Lab!
astra.act2.reboot_kit: Reboot Kit ready! We built it with the power core from that old weather probe. On Mars, nothing goes to waste.
astra.act2.surface_warning: Heads up! Outside, there's no soil above you, so radiation reaches you. Your HP will drop while you're out there. Rest brings your energy back, but real radiation adds up over time, so keep trips short.
astra.act2.title: ACT II: REACH OUT
astra.act3.blackbox_decode_start: Decoding the black box... Old code, new tricks. Got it! Playing Pathfinder-X's last log.
astra.act3.blackbox_react1: A thump every 37 minutes, like a clock. NASA's InSight lander felt more than 1,300 marsquakes, but quakes don't usually keep a schedule. Something down there is repeating.
astra.act3.blackbox_react2: And methane! On Earth, a lot of methane comes from living things, like microbes, tiny life too small to see. But it can also come from water reacting with certain rocks. NASA's Curiosity rover has sniffed methane on Mars too, and scientists are still working out where it comes from.
astra.act3.deep_scan: Deep Scan complete! The pulse comes from a pocket under the canyon floor. My readings say: salty liquid water. Salt helps water stay liquid even when it's very cold.
astra.act3.earth_reply: Message from Earth, sent {delay} ago: "Ares-Kids, this is Mission Control. We heard Pathfinder-X's log. Go find that signal, and stay safe!"
astra.act3.final_prep: This is it, Commander. The Rover is charged, your suit is sealed, and Earth is listening. Let's go find the Jezero Signal.
astra.act3.lab_built: Comms Lab online! Radio messages travel at the speed of light, the fastest thing there is. But Mars is so far away that a message takes between about 3 and 22 minutes to reach Earth. So no live video calls: we send video letters and wait.
astra.act3.lab_start: Pathfinder-X's antenna fits perfectly! Drone #01 is building the Research & Comms Lab.
astra.act3.ls_t2: Life Support upgraded! Mars air is mostly carbon dioxide, the gas we breathe out, and our new unit pulls oxygen from it. NASA's MOXIE made 122 grams of oxygen on Mars, about what a small dog breathes in 10 hours! And we melt ice to top up our water loop.
astra.act3.radiation_lesson: To explore farther, we need better shielding, stuff that blocks radiation. On Mars's surface, one day brings about as much radiation as three months of natural radiation on Earth. Packing soil around our rooms and the Rover blocks most of it.
astra.act3.rec_built: Recreation room open! In NASA's CHAPEA test, four volunteers lived for 378 days inside a 3D-printed pretend Mars home in Texas. Games, music and spare supplies helped them stay strong. Now we have them too!
astra.act3.roof_built: Regolith Roof Layer finished! Every room is now under thick soil, so it blocks most of the radiation. Scientists think a few meters of soil could protect real Mars bases.
astra.act3.title: ACT III: THE SIGNAL
astra.badge.first: Your first badge! Badges show the real things astronauts do to stay safe and do good science.
astra.char.bumble: Drone #02 likes to take its time and check everything. Meet "Bumble"!
astra.char.pip: Listen to those happy beeps! Let's call Drone #01 "Pip".
astra.char.zip: Whoa, Drone #03 is fast! We'll call it "Zip".
astra.coop.role_missing: Nobody on our crew is trained for this. You can still do it, it'll just take a bit longer.
astra.d1.a: Smart thinking! In 2018, a dust storm covered all of Mars and NASA's Opportunity rover ran out of power. Saving energy kept us safe.
astra.d1.alert: A giant dust storm is rolling across Jezero Crater! For 3 Sols, dust will block about 70% of our sunlight, and our dust-filter fans must work extra hard. Fun fact: dust storms make Mars days cooler and nights warmer. If we do nothing, our batteries could run dry, so how should we get ready?
astra.d1.b: Full batteries before a storm, just like charging a tablet before a long trip. A little radiation outside was worth it this time.
astra.d1.c: Oops, the storm drained our batteries. On Mars, the weather decides how much power we get. Next storm, let's prepare!
astra.d2.a: Water first! Without it, nothing else works. The space station recycles 98% of its water, and now so do we again.
astra.d2.alert: The water recycler's filter has cracked! We're getting back only 70% of our water instead of 98%. We have 12 Spare Parts: enough to fix the filter OR build a Cargo Trailer for the first Rover trip. Not both!
astra.d2.b: We spent parts to earn more parts. That's called investing! But wow, look how fast water vanishes at 70%. That's why 98% matters so much.
astra.d2.c: Using less is a real space trick: astronauts on the space station take sponge baths. It worked, but everyone felt a bit tired and grumpy.
astra.d3.a: The plants grew, but they soaked up perchlorates, salty chemicals that are bad for people. Good experiment: now we know! Scientists test things before they eat them.
astra.d3.alert: New idea from the crew: "Why not grow potatoes in Martian soil? It's free, and there's tons of it!" Hmm. Should we try it?
astra.d3.b: Perchlorates dissolve in water, so rinsing washes a lot of them out. But rinsing can leave some behind, so real scientists are still testing ways to make Mars soil safe for farms.
astra.d3.c: Safe choice! When you're not sure something is safe, testing first is what real scientists do.
astra.d4.a: Our plants are safe and cozy. Earth will still be there. Our next radio slot is in 3 Sols.
astra.d4.alert: A very cold night is coming, and the Greenhouse heater needs extra power. But tonight is also our first chance to send Pathfinder-X's log to Earth, and the Lab needs full power too. We can only do one!
astra.d4.b: Hearing from home made everyone smile! The plants got chilly, though. Most vegetables stop growing when it gets close to freezing.
astra.d4.c: Clever! We used heat that was already there. When two things need the same power, sometimes there's a third way.
astra.d5.a: Safety first! We left some treasure behind, but we can always go back. Astronauts never take chances with radiation.
astra.d5.alert: The Sun just shot out a burst of super-fast particles, a solar storm! The fastest particles can reach Mars in less than an hour, so we must decide fast! The base is well shielded under the soil, but the Rover crew is out at the Delta Cliffs. What should they do?
astra.d5.b: Thick rock blocks radiation, just like the soil over our base. Mars has very thin air and no magnetic shield around the whole planet, so we hide behind rock and dirt.
astra.d5.c: Our shielding helped a lot, but no shield blocks everything. We got the treasure, and now the crew needs a good rest.
astra.e1.a: Safe and sound! In May 2024, a huge solar storm hit Mars. NASA said an astronaut next to Curiosity would have got a dose like 30 chest X-rays at once.
astra.e1.alert: Solar flare! Its fastest particles can reach Mars in less than an hour. Our underground rooms are well shielded. Anyone outside or in an unfinished room will get a big dose of radiation, so what's the plan?
astra.e1.b: We kept working, but some of us took a hit. Next time, let's hide first and work later. Rest brings your energy back, but real radiation adds up over time, so it's better to avoid it.
astra.e1.c: That's what early warnings are for! Our drones are built to handle radiation better than people, but even robots can glitch in a big storm. In 2024, one storm knocked out the star camera on a spacecraft circling Mars for an hour!
astra.e1.watch: The Sun has a stormy spot facing Mars. A flare could come soon.
astra.e2.a.clean: Lucky! Dust devils sometimes cleaned the panels of NASA's Spirit and Opportunity rovers for free.
astra.e2.a.dusty: Not so lucky this time. Time to wipe!
astra.e2.alert: A dust devil, a spinning tornado of dust, is heading straight for our solar panels! It could blow the dust off, or dump a fresh load on them. What should we do?
astra.e2.b: Playing it safe. Stowed panels make less power, but they're safer from the dust.
astra.e2.c: Hands-on cleaning did the trick! A little time outside means a little radiation, so keep it short.
astra.e3.a: Found it! In 2020, the space station crew found a tiny leak by watching a floating tea leaf drift toward the hole!
astra.e3.alert: I hear a tiny hiss. There's a small air leak somewhere in the airlock! We're losing a bit of oxygen and water vapor every Sol. Let's find it!
astra.e3.b: Tape is a great quick fix, but it doesn't last forever. We'll need a proper repair soon.
astra.e3.c: Closing the door stops the leak while the drone works. Sometimes waiting is the safest move.
astra.e4.a: Happy plants! In 2016, astronaut Scott Kelly found moldy zinnia flowers on the space station. He cleaned them and nursed them back to health, and they bloomed!
astra.e4.alert: The plants look droopy! The nutrient mix in their water has drifted out of balance. Food output is down, and no fresh crops means less HP recovery.
astra.e4.b: Fresh water, fresh start. It cost some water, but the plants will bounce back by tomorrow.
astra.e4.c: Waiting made it worse. Plants without soil depend on us for all the minerals their roots need, so it's best to fix problems early.
astra.exp1.return: Weather probes measure wind, dust and temperature. This one got buried in the storm, but its power core still works. Let's use it to wake Drone #03!
astra.exp3.return: Mars has lots of frozen water, mostly underground and near the poles. Our scan found a small buried patch hiding in this cold shadow. Real ice this close to the equator would be a lucky find! Every Ice Core is 25 units of fresh water!
astra.exp4.at20: That's Ingenuity, the first helicopter to fly on another planet, in 2021. It made 72 flights! We look, but never touch. It's a piece of history.
astra.exp4.at35: Billions of years ago, a river flowed into a lake right here in Jezero Crater. This delta is the mud and sand it left behind. Mud is a great place to look for signs of ancient life.
astra.finale.closing: Real scientists are asking these same questions right now. Maybe one day, you'll be the one who answers them.
astra.finale.earth: Message from Earth, sent {delay} ago: "Ares-Kids, the whole world is cheering for you. Bring those samples home!"
astra.finale.home: Mission accomplished, Commander! You rebuilt a whole base and woke three drones. You found a salty spring next to what may be the oldest clues of life on Mars.
astra.finale.leopard: In 2024, NASA's Perseverance rover found a rock with spots just like these, here in Jezero Crater. It's called Cheyava Falls. In 2025, scientists said its spots are one of the best clues yet of ancient life on Mars. A clue, not proof, but a really good one!
astra.finale.methane: So where does the methane come from? Salty water reacting with rocks can make methane with no life at all. Or, long ago, tiny microbes might have made it. Only more clues can tell us which.
astra.fit.critical: Fitness is very low and it's hurting your health. Let's switch to the Recover plan.
astra.fit.intro: Exercise time! In low gravity, bones and muscles get weaker because they don't have to work as hard. Astronauts on the space station exercise about two hours every day.
astra.fit.low: Your muscles are getting weak, and that makes work and trips harder. Add an exercise hour to your Sol Plan!
astra.fit.mars: Mars gravity is 38% of Earth's. Scientists don't know yet how much bone and muscle people would lose here, so we keep exercising to be safe.
astra.fit.rec_open: The Recreation room has an exercise bike and a weight machine, like the ones on the space station. Your workouts count double now!
astra.hp.25: HP is low! Let's get you somewhere safe. Rest and fresh food will restore your energy.
astra.hp.50: HP is at half. Time to head home soon, or take a rest in the Bedroom.
astra.hp.full: HP back to 100! You're ready for anything.
astra.hp.medrest_end: Good morning! You're rested and back at 50 HP. Eat something fresh to get stronger.
astra.hp.surface_70: Your HP is dropping out here. Radiation adds up, so don't stay longer than you need.
astra.hp.zero_base: You're worn out. Into Med-Rest Mode for 1 Sol. The drones and I will keep things running. See you tomorrow!
astra.hp.zero_expedition: Your HP hit zero, so I'm sending a rescue drone. It will bring you and some of the loot home safely.
astra.intro.landing: Touchdown confirmed! Welcome to Ares-1, our station in Jezero Crater. I'm ASTRA 6.7, your station AI. Gravity here is only 38% of Earth's, so try not to bounce into the ceiling!
astra.intro.status: Good news: the Bedroom, Kitchen and Life Support work. Bad news: everything on the right is just steel frames, and our solar panels are buried in dust.
astra.intro.why_underground: Our base is built underground, under a thick blanket of Martian soil. Space radiation is invisible energy that zooms in from the Sun and deep space. Mars has very thin air and no magnetic shield around the whole planet, so space radiation reaches the ground. The soil above us blocks most of it.
astra.logbook.first: That fact went into your Science Logbook! Every real fact you learn on Mars becomes a card.
astra.mg.air_filter_scrub: Every time someone comes in from outside, tiny dust grains ride in on their spacesuit. Clean filters keep that dust out of your lungs.
astra.mg.dish_antenna_alignment: Radio waves travel at the speed of light. Still, a message takes about 3 to 22 minutes to cross between Mars and Earth. Point the dish just right, or the message misses Earth completely!
astra.mg.heat_pump_reroute: Mars nights can drop to about minus 80 degrees Celsius. We send leftover heat through pipes to where it's needed, just like NASA's Perseverance rover does to stay warm.
astra.mg.nutrient_match: Plants mostly use red and blue light, so our LEDs shine those colors and the Greenhouse glows purple. Without soil, the water must carry all the minerals their roots need, so we check it often.
astra.mg.solar_wipe: Mars dust is full of static electricity, so it clings to panels like socks to a sweater. Dust on its solar panels is what ended NASA's InSight lander mission in 2022.
astra.mg.suit_seal_check: Mars air is about 100 times thinner than Earth's, so without a sealed suit you couldn't breathe out there. Your radiation badge counts how much space radiation you get, just like the badges real astronauts wear.
astra.mg.valve_balance: Every breath you breathe out has carbon dioxide in it, and too much makes people sleepy and sick. Our scrubbers grab it. Then our machine pulls oxygen out of Mars's carbon dioxide air, just like NASA's MOXIE did.
astra.mg.water_sort: On the space station, sweat, breath and even pee get cleaned back into drinking water. About 98% of it comes back. That last 2% is why we still need ice from the Rover.
astra.mg.wheel_pebble_vacuum: Sharp, pointy rocks poked holes in NASA's Curiosity rover's metal wheels. A quick clean and check now saves a long walk later!
astra.plan.crunch: Crunch mode! We'll build faster, but the crew will feel it. Let's not do this every Sol.
astra.plan.no_free: No free time at all? Everybody needs a break, even on Mars.
astra.plan.override: No problem, let's do it now! You'll miss that hour of {block}, so its bonus is skipped today.
astra.plan.short_sleep: Less sleep means more work time, but you'll get tired and grumpy. Astronauts protect their sleep.
astra.plan.unlock: Good morning! Real astronauts follow a daily plan: work, meals, sleep and exercise. Tap your portrait to see your Sol Plan.
astra.rad.partial_room: This room's roof isn't finished yet, so a little radiation gets in. Don't hang around here too long!
astra.rad.rover_shield: We packed Martian soil bricks around the Rover cabin. Mars soil cuts the radiation a lot, and there's plenty of it!
astra.rad.suit_liner: New suit liner! Materials full of hydrogen, like water and some plastics, are great at blocking space radiation.
astra.report.intro: Here's how our mission went, Commander. Every choice taught us something.
astra.report.outro: Real scientists write reports like this after every mission. Then they plan the next one even better.
astra.res.emergency_worry: The base is in trouble and the crew is getting worried. Let's fix it soon!
astra.res.food_low: Food stores are low. Check the Greenhouse, and keep those plants happy!
astra.res.heat_zero: Heat emergency! The pipes are freezing. Reroute the heat pump now, and grab a blanket!
astra.res.morale_low: The crew is feeling down. A visit to the Recreation room or a message from Earth would help.
astra.res.oxygen_low: Oxygen is getting low. Let's check the air scrubbers, the machines that clean our air!
astra.res.oxygen_zero: Oxygen emergency! Everyone into the Bedroom, it has backup air tanks. Once we're safe, I'll show you how to fix the scrubber.
astra.res.power_zero: Power emergency! I've switched off everything except life support. Let's get the panels clean.
astra.res.storage_save: Good thing we packed spares! I opened the emergency stores.
astra.res.water_low: Water is running low. Our water recycler cleans and reuses 98%, but we still lose a little every day. Time for an Ice Run!
astra.sandbox.milestone_50: Fifty Sols on Mars! Real Mars missions plan for stays of more than a year. You're getting there!
astra.sandbox.random_tip: Tip: the Ice Run and the Scrap Run never run out. Use them whenever water or spare parts get low.
astra.sandbox.start: Free-Play Mode unlocked! The base is yours. Build, grow, explore and keep everyone healthy. I'll be right here.
astra.t2.battery: Deep Cell Bank charged! More stored power means more warmth through long, freezing nights.
astra.t2.garage: With this battery, the Rover can go farther than ever. NASA's Opportunity rover drove about 45 kilometers on Mars, more than a marathon!
astra.t2.greenhouse: Vertical LED Farm growing! Stacking trays grows more food in the same small room. Every bit of space counts on Mars!
astra.t2.lab: Deep Space Array online! Now we can spot storms early and scan deep underground.
astra.t2.rec: We put a real Mars rock on display! Looking at something beautiful helps the crew feel at home.
astra.t2.solar: New panels with brushes and a tilt motor! Gusts of wind sometimes cleaned the solar panels of NASA's Spirit and Opportunity rovers. But we'd rather not wait for luck.
astra.t2.workshop: Precision Fabricator online! It's like the 3D printer on the space station, but bigger. Now we can make two things each Sol.
astra.tut.build_prompt: Tap the Battery & Heating frame, then tap Build. Drone #01 will do the rest.
astra.tut.done: Perfect! Builds take a few Sols. A Sol is one Mars day, and it's 39 minutes longer than a day on Earth.
astra.tut.drone01_click: That's Drone #01, fast asleep. Its battery is empty, and our solar panels are buried in dust. Let's clean them first!
astra.tut.drone01_prompt: Panels are working! Now drag the charged battery into Drone #01's back hatch and snap the cable in.
astra.tut.drone01_wake: Beep-boop! Drone #01 is awake. Drones can't talk, but they never get tired. Let's give it a job: the base is getting cold.
astra.tut.hp_intro: This green bar is your HP, your health and energy. Hard work and radiation lower it. Sleep and fresh food restore your energy. Real radiation adds up over time, so astronauts limit their time outside.
astra.tut.solar_done: Sunlight is flowing! Mars gets less than half the sunlight Earth does, so every clean panel matters.
astra.tut.solar_prompt: First job: clean the solar panels. Mars dust is sticky with static, so wipe it off!
badge.air_from_mars.name: Air From Mars
badge.air_from_mars.text: You made oxygen from Mars air, like NASA's MOXIE.
badge.biosignature_hunter.name: Biosignature Hunter
badge.biosignature_hunter.text: You brought home samples that might hold clues to ancient life.
badge.closed_loop.name: Closed Loop
badge.closed_loop.text: Your recycler saved 98% of the water for 10 Sols in a row.
badge.first_contact.name: Message in Minutes
badge.first_contact.text: You sent your first message across millions of kilometers to Earth.
badge.flare_safe.name: No HP Lost in a Solar Flare
badge.flare_safe.text: Your crew sheltered every time, so no flare cost more than the tiny shelter dose.
badge.forecaster.name: Space Weather Forecaster
badge.forecaster.text: You used a flare forecast to shelter at just the right time.
badge.ice_miner.name: Ice Miner
badge.ice_miner.text: You melted 5 Ice Cores into fresh water.
badge.look_dont_touch.name: Look, Don't Touch
badge.look_dont_touch.text: You visited Ingenuity and left it just as you found it.
badge.panel_sweeper.name: Panel Sweeper
badge.panel_sweeper.text: You cleaned the solar panels 5 times.
badge.perchlorate_wash.name: Washed the Perchlorates
badge.perchlorate_wash.text: You rinsed a lot of the salty perchlorates out of Mars soil before growing food.
badge.space_gardener.name: Space Gardener
badge.space_gardener.text: You grew 50 Food in the Greenhouse.
badge.storm_ready.name: Storm Ready
badge.storm_ready.text: You got ready before the dust storm arrived.
badge.strong_bones.name: Strong Bones
badge.strong_bones.text: You kept your crew fit for 10 Sols in a row.
badge.under_the_blanket.name: Under the Blanket
badge.under_the_blanket.text: You covered every room with thick soil to block radiation.
badge.well_rested.name: Well Rested
badge.well_rested.text: You slept a full 8 hours every Sol of your first week.
card.ancient_lake.text: Billions of years ago, a river flowed into a lake in Jezero Crater and built a delta. Its old mud is a top place to look for signs of past life.
card.ancient_lake.title: Ancient Lake
card.blue_sunset.text: Near the setting Sun, Mars's sky glows blue, while Earth's sunsets are orange. Scientists think fine dust scattering light causes it.
card.blue_sunset.title: Blue Sunsets
card.brine.text: Salts like perchlorate lower the temperature at which water freezes. Tiny amounts of salty water may form in Martian soil on some nights.
card.brine.title: Salty Water
card.chapea.text: In NASA's CHAPEA test, four volunteers lived 378 days in a 3D-printed habitat in Houston. They practised life on Mars.
card.chapea.title: Pretend Mars Home
card.cliff_shelter.text: Cliffs and lava tubes could give astronauts extra shielding in a solar storm. Rock works like the soil over a base.
card.cliff_shelter.title: Cliff Shelter
card.cold_nights.text: Perseverance measured minus 83 °C one night in Jezero Crater. Rovers and bases must keep warm to survive.
card.cold_nights.title: Freezing Nights
card.dose_adds_up.text: Radiation dose adds up over an astronaut's whole career. NASA's limit is 600 millisieverts for a lifetime of spaceflight.
card.dose_adds_up.title: Dose Adds Up
card.dust_devils.text: In March 2005, passing dust devils cleaned Spirit's solar panels. Its power jumped from about 60% to 93%.
card.dust_devils.title: Dust Devil Cleaners
card.dust_hitchhikers.text: Fine dust sticks to spacesuits and can ride inside the base. The tiniest grains can reach deep into the lungs.
card.dust_hitchhikers.title: Dust Hitchhikers
card.fast_particles.text: In May 2024, particles from a solar storm reached Mars in just tens of minutes. That leaves little time to take shelter.
card.fast_particles.title: Fast Particles
card.flare_forecast.text: Flares start in active regions, magnetic hot spots on the Sun. Forecasters give the chance of a flare, not its exact time.
card.flare_forecast.title: Space Weather Forecast
card.global_storms.text: Some Martian dust storms grow until they circle the whole planet. NASA called the 2018 storm "planet-encircling".
card.global_storms.title: Planet-Wide Storms
card.gravity.text: Mars pulls on you with 38% of Earth's gravity. You could jump about two and a half times higher there!
card.gravity.title: Mars Gravity
card.green_air.text: Plants use light to turn carbon dioxide and water into food and oxygen. Scientists have tested plants for space life support since the 1950s and 60s.
card.green_air.title: Green Air
card.hidden_ice.text: Mars has lots of frozen water near the poles and under the ground in the mid-latitudes. NASA maps it to choose landing sites for astronauts.
card.hidden_ice.title: Hidden Ice
card.hydrogen_shield.text: Materials rich in hydrogen, like water and some plastics, are good at blocking space radiation. Liquid hydrogen is best, but hard to use.
card.hydrogen_shield.title: Hydrogen Shield
card.ingenuity.text: Ingenuity first flew on April 19, 2021, the first aircraft on another world. It made 72 flights before its mission ended in 2024.
card.ingenuity.title: First Mars Helicopter
card.insight_dust.text: Dust slowly covered InSight's solar panels until its batteries ran out. NASA ended the mission in December 2022.
card.insight_dust.title: Dusty Panels
card.last_storm.text: In June 2018, a Mars-wide dust storm blocked the sunlight Opportunity needed for power. The rover fell silent and was never heard from again.
card.last_storm.title: Opportunity's Last Storm
card.leopard_spots.text: In 2024, Perseverance found a rock with light spots ringed in dark material. NASA calls them a possible sign of past life: a clue, not proof.
card.leopard_spots.title: Leopard Spots
card.long_stay.text: NASA's human mission studies plan about 500 days on the surface of Mars. That's longer than a year on Earth.
card.long_stay.title: A Long Stay
card.mars_gravity_body.text: Nobody knows yet how much bone and muscle people would lose in Mars gravity. In a lab model, rats carrying 40% of their weight lost grip strength in two weeks.
card.mars_gravity_body.title: Unknown at 38%
card.marsquakes.text: NASA's InSight lander detected 1,319 marsquakes. Some were caused by space rocks hitting Mars.
card.marsquakes.title: Marsquakes
card.methane.text: Curiosity has detected methane in Mars's air, and the amount changes. It could come from rocks and water, or from life, and nobody knows yet.
card.methane.title: Mystery Gas
card.moxie.text: NASA's MOXIE made 122 grams of oxygen from Mars's carbon dioxide air. That's about what a small dog breathes in 10 hours.
card.moxie.title: Air From Mars
card.no_shield.text: Mars lost its planet-wide magnetic field billions of years ago. Only small magnetic patches remain in its crust.
card.no_shield.title: No Global Shield
card.no_showers.text: Space station crews can't shower, because water is limited and floats around. They wash with towels and rinseless shampoo.
card.no_showers.title: No Showers in Space
card.perchlorates.text: In 2008, NASA's Phoenix lander found perchlorate salts in Martian soil. In people, it can upset the thyroid, a small gland in the neck that helps the body grow.
card.perchlorates.title: Perchlorates
card.plants_soak.text: Lettuce grown in water with perchlorate stores some of it in its leaves. That's why soil and water are tested before growing food.
card.plants_soak.title: Plants Soak It Up
card.printed_wrench.text: In 2014, a 3D printer on the space station made a wrench from a file sent up from Earth. Printing took about four hours.
card.printed_wrench.title: Printed in Space
card.purple_garden.text: Plants use mostly red and blue light and reflect green. That's why space gardens under LEDs glow pink and purple.
card.purple_garden.title: Purple Gardens
card.radiation_badge.text: Astronauts wear radiation badges, called dosimeters, that add up the radiation they receive. It is a NASA rule for every crew member.
card.radiation_badge.title: Radiation Badge
card.rock_pages.text: Rock layers stack up over time, with the oldest at the bottom. Curiosity reads them to learn about ancient lakes and rivers.
card.rock_pages.title: Rock Pages
card.rover_marathon.text: In 2015, Opportunity passed a full marathon distance of 42.195 kilometers. By the end it had driven more than 45 kilometers.
card.rover_marathon.title: Rover Marathon
card.sealed_samples.text: Perseverance seals rock cores in airtight titanium tubes. They wait on Mars so they could be collected in the future.
card.sealed_samples.title: Sealed Samples
card.sharp_rocks.text: Sharp Martian rocks punched holes in the thin aluminum skin of Curiosity's wheels. Drivers now choose smoother routes.
card.sharp_rocks.title: Sharp Rocks
card.sleep_missions.text: Astronauts follow strict sleep schedules, even before launch. Too little sleep leads to tired mistakes.
card.sleep_missions.title: Sleep in Space
card.slow_messages.text: Radio waves are as fast as light. Still, a message between Mars and Earth takes about 3 to 22 minutes, depending on where the planets are.
card.slow_messages.title: Slow Messages
card.soil_blanket.text: Soil overhead blocks a lot of space radiation. Scientists calculate that about 1 to 2.5 meters would protect a Mars base.
card.soil_blanket.title: Soil Blanket
card.soil_wash.text: Perchlorate dissolves easily in water, but rinsing soil can leave some behind. Scientists are still testing ways to make Mars soil safe for farms.
card.soil_wash.title: Washing Soil
card.sol.text: A day on Mars is called a sol. It lasts 24 hours, 39 minutes and 35 seconds.
card.sol.title: One Sol
card.space_flowers.text: In 2016, zinnias on the space station grew mold after too much water and too little airflow. Scott Kelly cleaned them and they bloomed.
card.space_flowers.title: Space Flowers
card.space_salad.text: On August 10, 2015, astronauts on the space station ate red romaine lettuce grown on board. It was the first station-grown crop on the menu.
card.space_salad.title: Space Salad
card.stacked_farm.text: Vertical farms grow plants on shelves stacked high. One two-acre indoor farm grows about as much as a 720-acre outdoor farm.
card.stacked_farm.title: Stacked Farms
card.sticky_dust.text: Martian dust picks up electric charge when grains rub together. The charge makes it cling to solar panels and windows.
card.sticky_dust.title: Sticky Dust
card.storm_temps.text: In a dust storm, Mars days get cooler because less sunlight reaches the ground. Nights get warmer because the dusty air heats the ground.
card.storm_temps.title: Warm Stormy Nights
card.strong_in_space.text: In space, the bones that carry your weight get about 1% less solid each month without exercise. So station crews exercise about two hours a day.
card.strong_in_space.title: Strong in Space
card.sunlight.text: Mars is farther from the Sun, so it gets about 43% of Earth's sunlight. Solar panels must be big and clean.
card.sunlight.title: Weaker Sunshine
card.surface_dose.text: Curiosity measured how much radiation reaches the Martian surface each day. People in the US get about that much from nature in three months.
card.surface_dose.title: A Day of Radiation
card.tea_leaves.text: In 2020, a Russian astronaut on the space station let tea leaves float in a sealed room. The leaves drifted toward a tiny air leak.
card.tea_leaves.title: Tea Leaf Detective
card.thin_air.text: Mars's air is about 100 times thinner than Earth's. Without a pressure suit, you couldn't breathe outside.
card.thin_air.title: Thin Air
card.thirty_xrays.text: On May 20, 2024, Curiosity measured a huge radiation spike. An astronaut there would have got a dose like 30 chest X-rays.
card.thirty_xrays.title: 30 Chest X-rays
card.too_much_co2.text: Every breath out adds carbon dioxide to a closed room. Too much causes headaches and tiredness, so scrubbers remove it.
card.too_much_co2.title: Too Much CO₂
card.waste_heat.text: Perseverance's power generator makes extra heat. Warm fluid carries it around the rover to protect its electronics at night.
card.waste_heat.title: Waste Heat
card.water_98.text: The space station recovers about 98% of its water, including from sweat, breath and urine. Every drop counts in space.
card.water_98.title: 98% Recycled
card.weather_station.text: Perseverance's MEDA measures temperature, wind, air pressure, dampness and dust. It even measures the size and shape of dust grains.
card.weather_station.title: Mars Weather Station
card.wet_soil.text: Future Mars bases could pile soil on top to block radiation. Soil with water in it works even better, because hydrogen helps.
card.wet_soil.title: Building With Soil
card.wind_ripples.text: Gentle Martian winds shape sand into ripples, and faster winds build dunes. Their shapes help scientists study Mars's winds.
card.wind_ripples.title: Wind Ripples
char.astro_botanist.bio: Sofía grew up on a vineyard in Chile and studied plants in deserts. She names every lettuce in the Greenhouse. Wrenches are not her friends.
char.astro_botanist.name: Sofía Ramírez
char.chief_engineer.bio: Kenji built robots in a Tokyo workshop as a teenager. He talks to machines while he fixes them. He has never met a plant that liked him.
char.chief_engineer.name: Kenji Mori
char.chief_engineer.trait: If it's broken, it's just a puzzle.
char.commander.bio: Amara flew cargo planes over the Sahara before training for Mars. She can fix a pump, cook a stew and calm a worried crew. Her favourite tool is a checklist.
char.commander.name: Amara Eze
char.commander.trait: We plan, we try, we learn. Then we try again.
char.comms_officer.bio: Noor tracked satellites from a desert radio station in Jordan. She hears space weather coming before anyone else. Outside, she would rather stay in the Rover.
char.comms_officer.name: Noor Haddad
char.comms_officer.trait: Listen first. The Sun always gives clues.
char.mission_control.bio: Rosa is the CAPCOM: the one voice that talks to the crew from Earth. She has guided spacecraft for thirty years. Her messages arrive minutes late, but always with a smile.
char.mission_control.name: Rosa Varga
char.rover_pilot.bio: Leo drove rally cars and studied rocks in the Carpathian Mountains. He can read a cliff like a storybook. He always comes home hungry.
char.rover_pilot.name: Leo Petrenko
char.rover_pilot.trait: Every rock has a story. Let's go find it!
crawl.02: A robot scout named PATHFINDER-X is exploring Jezero Crater on Mars.
crawl.03: Deep inside a canyon, it feels something strange. A thump in the ground... every 37 minutes.
crawl.04: Then its nose sniffs a sudden puff of methane gas.
crawl.05: A giant dust storm rolls in. Pathfinder-X goes silent.
crawl.07: Builder drones were sent ahead to dig an underground base. But a new storm buried them too.
crawl.08: Now it's your turn. Land. Wake the drones. Find the signal.
log.pathfinder.02: Seismic pulse detected. Interval: 37 minutes. Repeating.
log.pathfinder.03: Methane spike: 40 parts per billion. Source: canyon floor, 18 kilometers west.
log.pathfinder.04: Warning: dust storm approaching. Switching to sleep mo—
radio.exp1.00: Rover rolling! Destination: weather probe Breeze-7, 3 kilometers east.
radio.exp1.100: Heading home. Put the kettle on, ASTRA!
radio.exp1.30: Driving over sand ripples. Mars wind shaped these, just like dunes on Earth.
radio.exp1.60: Found it! Breeze-7 is half buried in dust. Digging it out.
radio.exp1.80: Got its power core and a bag of parts. The core still has a little charge!
radio.exp2.00: Rover rolling north. Titanium wheels ready for the boulder field.
radio.exp2.100: Pathfinder-X, you did great. We'll take it from here. Heading home!
radio.exp2.25: Boulders everywhere! Weaving between them slowly.
radio.exp2.50: I see a mast sticking out of the dust... It's Pathfinder-X!
radio.exp2.60: The black box is under a heavy solar panel. How should we get it out?
radio.exp2.80: Black box secured. Unbolting its big dish antenna too.
radio.exp3.00: Rover heading for the crater rim. It's steep up there.
radio.exp3.100: Bringing home enough water for weeks!
radio.exp3.30: Climbing slowly. The rim casts a long, cold shadow.
radio.exp3.70: ICE! Clear and sparkly. Filling the cargo box.
radio.exp4.00: Long trip ahead! Radiation shielding packed, suit liner on.
radio.exp4.100: Heading home with the best haul yet!
radio.exp4.20: Look left: a little helicopter sitting on a hill. It's Ingenuity!
radio.exp4.35: Reached the delta cliffs. You can see layers of old mud and sand.
radio.exp4.50: Camping in the Rover tonight. Goodnight, base!
radio.exp4.80: Found shiny battery cells in an old supply cache, and some beautiful rocks.
radio.exp5.01: RADIO: Rover leaving the airlock. Destination: the Canyon Anomaly.
radio.exp5.02: RADIO: Entering the canyon. The walls are made of layers, like a giant stack of pancakes. Each layer is a page of Mars history.
radio.exp5.03: RADIO: The ground is rumbling. Next pulse in 3... 2... 1...
radio.exp5.04: RADIO: Whoa! A puff of salty water vapor just burst out of a crack and froze into sparkly frost!
radio.exp5.05: RADIO: Look at the rock beside the crack. Tiny dark rings with light centers, like leopard spots!
radio.exp5.06: RADIO: Samples sealed in tubes, just like Perseverance does. Heading home!
radio.run.50.1: Found a few bolts and a bent panel.
radio.run.50.3: Lots of dust today, driving slow.
report.no_flare_loss: Nobody took more than the tiny shelter dose from a solar flare. Great planning!
report.rating.base.1: You got the base working! Next time, try waking the drones early to build faster.
report.rating.base.2: Good building! Next time, try keeping all three drones busy.
report.rating.base.3: Great job! You finished the whole station and upgraded it.
report.rating.crew.1: You kept everyone going! Next time, try more sleep and an exercise hour each Sol.
report.rating.crew.2: Good care! Next time, try the Recover plan after hard days.
report.rating.crew.3: Great job! Your crew stayed healthy, fit and happy.
report.rating.science.1: You learned real Mars science! Next time, try visiting more places with the Rover.
report.rating.science.2: Good exploring! Next time, try new choices to find more science cards.
report.rating.science.3: Great job! You're a real Mars scientist.
report.rating.title: MISSION RATING
report.title: MISSION REPORT — ARES-1
